xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5178: Dashboard stalls ~1.5 s whenever a tab connects to /ws/rpc (first snapshot blocks the event loop?)

plan.title: Dashboard stalls ~1.5 s whenever a tab connects to /ws/rpc (first snapshot blocks the event loop?)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: A deep-linked issue drawer shows its loading title for about 2.2 s. Planning measured the cause: it is not the /ws/rpc snapshot. The drawer's GET /api/issues/:id (1-10 ms of server time) and the session mint POST /api/dashboard/session are issued last in a burst of about 45 REST requests sent in one React commit. On HTTP/1.1 (localhost:3011, desktop shell) Chromium sends 6 at a time, so they wait 1.1-2.3 s in the browser behind slow status reads. On HTTP/2 (Traefik) they reach a busy server last (TTFB 1.0-1.4 s). /ws/rpc sends no RPC until the session mint returns, so the snapshot waits too. The snapshot path itself is about 60-70 ms (handler 3-11 ms, encode plus stringify plus TextEncoder 49-59 ms for 5.5 MB).
narratives.Proposal: Send the session mint and, on a deep link, the issue record read from a new src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/bootRequests.ts called in main.tsx before React renders, so both leave the browser first (measured: 41-52 ms and 108-121 ms on both origins). Memoize the server's cleanIssues deep copy by input-array identity so repeated getSnapshot calls stop re-cleaning 5 MB. Add an event-loop delay test for getSnapshot with 1,500 issues (max under 100 ms), a committed Playwright latency script with --assert, and docs plus a changelog entry. A final item serves the branch frontend with Vite and runs the latency script with --assert. Server-side burst congestion is PAN-5180.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Making the slow status endpoints fast (/api/prerequisites, /api/claude-code/status, /api/flywheel/status, /api/workspace-registry, /api/conversations/pending-input) and the server-side congestion of the whole tab-open burst (PAN-5180)
- Removing description from the snapshot or changing the snapshot wire format, schema or RPC
- Pre-serializing, chunking or streaming the snapshot
- Marking other boot fetches priority low, or deduplicating repeated boot reads such as /api/settings
- The dashboard's background CPU use and its chronic event-loop p99 warnings
- Pruning stopped agents from agentsById
- Prefetching for the cockpit route /command-deck/<project>/<issue>
- Serving the dashboard over HTTP/2 on port 3011
- Raising any test threshold to make a test pass
- Making the first connect after a server start (JIT warm-up) fit under 100 ms; it has its own 300 ms limit (NFR-1b)

autoDecisions.summary: Fix request ordering instead of the snapshot path; keep both of the issue's acceptance criteria.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue marks its hypothesis unconfirmed and makes Confirm step 1. Measurement showed the issue read queued 1,094-2,348 ms with 3-72 ms TTFB on HTTP/1.1, and 1,008 ms TTFB behind the burst on HTTP/2. The snapshot path was 60-70 ms. Firing the two requests at domcontentloaded brought them to 41-52 ms and 108-121 ms. The acceptance criteria are outcomes, so they still bind.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not mark other boot fetches priority low.
autoDecisions.rationale: Tested in Chromium: priority high on the critical fetch did nothing, and priority low works only when every other boot fetch (30+ call sites) carries it. A future fetch without it silently regresses. Issuing first is one module.

autoDecisions.summary: The issue's Playwright check is a committed script (scripts/verify-deep-link-latency.mjs --assert), run by the test role against a branch build in an isolated browser.
autoDecisions.rationale: The existing e2e harness replaces window.fetch, so a CI spec cannot observe the browser connection queue. This follows scripts/verify-dashboard-performance.mjs and the PAN-5171 D-14 split.

autoDecisions.summary: The event-loop test uses RpcGroup.make(GetSnapshotRpc) over the real RpcServer and JSON serialization, with a real ReadModelServiceLive, and a fixture of 1,500 issues (2,400-character descriptions) plus 100 agents.
autoDecisions.rationale: Mounting websocketRpcRouteLayer needs EventStoreService, TerminalService and PanOpen stubs; the production handler only adds logging around the same readModel.getSnapshot call. The acceptance criterion names 1,500 issues; agent volume is a separate concern.

autoDecisions.summary: Memoize cleanIssues by input-array identity with a WeakMap.
autoDecisions.rationale: IssueDataService.getIssues() returns one cached array until the next poll, getSnapshot runs on every connect and every 500 ms while an issue stream is open, and reducers never mutate issuesRaw rows in place.

autoDecisions.summary: This issue fixes the deep-linked drawer and the session mint only; the server-side congestion of the tab-open burst (late requests wait 1.0-1.4 s TTFB on HTTP/2, other clients' pings stall 280-433 ms) and the slow status endpoints are filed as PAN-5180.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's headline says other clients stall when a tab opens. Planning confirmed that, but the cause is the whole burst on a busy server, not the snapshot, and fixing it means profiling and caching several unrelated endpoints.

autoDecisions.summary: The work agent verifies the fix itself by serving the branch frontend with Vite (proxied to the running dashboard) and running the latency script with --assert; the test role repeats it in its own isolated browser.
autoDecisions.rationale: WI-1 and WI-2 change only the frontend, Vite's dev proxy targets 127.0.0.1:3011 by default, and Vite serves HTTP/1.1, so the browser's 6-request limit applies. No branch-built dashboard server is needed.

autoDecisions.summary: Critique round 1 accepted: valid shared-route fixture (#/shared/bcdf-ghjk), issue-read recovery after the session settles (FR-7), histogram kept on through one timer turn plus a detection self-check, and NFR-1 split into warm (100 ms) and first-connect (300 ms) limits.
autoDecisions.rationale: Each finding was verified against the code: sharedRouteCode needs 8 characters, TanStack Query fires the query function before the mint's microtask, monitorEventLoopDelay records only when its timer fires, and the cold encode at production volume is 91-96 ms.

Event-loop delay test for a getSnapshot connect with 1,500 issues

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-4 and D-9, D-9a, D-9c. Write bootSnapshotServer(agentCount) from the read-model-served-agent-status.test.ts and ws-rpc-revoke.test.ts patterns, serving RpcGroup.make(GetSnapshotRpc) whose 'pan.getSnapshot' handler returns readModel.getSnapshot over RpcServer.toHttpEffectWebsocket with RpcSerialization.layerJson, with 1,500 fixture issues (2,400-character descriptions). Write connectAndSnapshot (never JSON.parse inside), measured (monitorEventLoopDelay resolution 1, enable, await, one 20 ms setTimeout measurement turn, disable) and busyWait. Declare three tests in order: first connect with 1,700 agents under 300 ms with all 1,500 issues in the reply; warm connects with 100 agents (one warm-up, three measured, smallest max under 100 ms); and a self-check that an injected 120 ms block reports max at least 100. No fake timers and no other waits. Run the implementation checkpoint and record values in the PR body.

items.title: Given a fresh test process with 1,500 issues and 1,700 agents, when the first ws client completes pan.getSnapshot, then the measured event-loop max is under 300 ms and the reply parses to an Exit Success with 1,500 issues
Given 1,500 issues, 100 agents and one warm-up connect, when three measured connects complete pan.getSnapshot, then the smallest event-loop max is under 100 ms
Given an injected 120 ms synchronous block inside a measured window, then the harness reports a max of at least 100 ms

The test file contains no vi.useFakeTimers call, its only timer wait is the 20 ms measurement turn in measured(), and the PR body records the values from 5 local runs and whether the setImmediate fallback was applied
Committed Playwright deep-link latency check script

expected_outputs: one 'run 1:' line with total=, queued=, ttfb= and title at dcl+

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-5. Write scripts/verify-deep-link-latency.mjs in the argument style of scripts/verify-dashboard-performance.mjs. It reads the internal token from OVERDECK_HOME or ~/.overdeck, reads the real title through GET /api/issues/<ID>, then per run launches Chromium with a fresh context carrying the x-overdeck-internal-token header, opens <base>/?issue=<ID>, and records domcontentloaded, the first /api/issues/<ID> request's total, queued and ttfb timing, the time the issue-drawer test id contains the real title, and the first five /api/ request paths. It prints one line per run and, with --assert, exits 1 when the issue read is 300 ms or more or the title appears 1,000 ms or more after domcontentloaded.
